items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

ctx.x: reasons that I left the business world, left Stanford, was something that I actually had seen at Allstate while I was there. I was there from ’68 to ’70, for two years, and I left because I could not believe the short attention span that was now developing in American business. When I first got to Allstate in ’68 one of the most important parts of the company in their planning effort was they looked at a five year plan and a ten year plan, and those — the five year plan was in service of the ten year plan so the…

resisted as long as they could but they’re — and it’s not even about money either, that’s what makes it so sad, because ultimately it’s really not about how much we made or how much we didn’t make, it’s really about how much did we give to our stockholders. And that’s such a game that’s being played. I mean we see the results of that game, and right now there’s a big cover-up going on because it’s not about what happened to Enron and those guys it’s about what’s going on with the rest of all these jacklays, as…
Can you tell me, is there a spiritual side to your music? A spiritual element?
